passage:
"Sit and pray with us, Tushar," said Dadi, patting the mat.
Tushar sat down, folded his hands like his sister Ganga, and shut his eyes when she did.
"Dadi, why do we ring the bell?"
"Good question, beta. The sound tells us it is prayer time, and it helps us feel quiet. Some people like it, some don't."
"Can I ring it?"
"After the prayer. Come, sit near me."
He leaned against her shawl, warm and sleepy, and hummed along with the words he did not know.

qa.q: What did Tushar ask Dadi about?
qa.a: Tushar asked why they ring the bell.

qa.q: How does Tushar feel while leaning against Dadi's shawl?
qa.a: He seems warm, safe and part of the family: he leans on her and hums along even though he does not know the words.

qa.q: What did Dadi do that a wise elder would do?
qa.a: She welcomed his question and explained simply instead of telling him to be quiet, and she promised he could ring the bell afterwards.

qa.q: How does Dadi see Tushar's question about the bell?
qa.a: She calls it a good question and answers gently, so she seems to see it as welcome curiosity and not as disrespect.

grounding: Tushar prays at Dadi's request without knowing why, feels loved, and Dadi welcomes his 'why'.

passage: In the Berlin flat, Babaanne spread the prayer mats in the evening. "Zeynep, come, sit and pray with us." Zeynep put down her doll and sat beside her grandmother. She copied everything: hands up, bow, sit. She didn't know the words, but Babaanne's shoulder was warm against hers. Afterwards Zeynep asked, "Babaanne, why do we bow?" Her uncle frowned. "Don't ask, just do it." But Babaanne laughed and pulled Zeynep onto her lap. "Good question! We bow to say God is great and we are thankful. Ask me anything, canım." Zeynep asked three more questions.

qa.q: What did Zeynep put down before sitting to pray?
How did Zeynep feel sitting beside Babaanne?
qa.a: She felt loved and part of the family, warm against her grandmother's shoulder even without knowing the words.

qa.q: Why was Babaanne's reply wiser than the uncle's?
qa.a: She welcomed Zeynep's why and explained simply, so the prayer began to have meaning instead of being only an order.

qa.q: How might Babaanne feel when Zeynep asks three more questions?
qa.a: She probably feels delighted and close to her granddaughter, glad to share what the prayers mean. 😊

grounding: A young girl joins her grandmother's prayers without knowing why, feels loved, and her grandmother welcomes her questions.

passage: In the hospital room, Dadi sat up in bed with her prayer beads. "Jagdish, beta, sit and pray with us." Jagdish climbed onto the chair and folded his hands like Dadi. He did not know why, but Dadi smiled at him, and he liked that. Afterwards he whispered, "Dadi, why do we pray in the hospital?" Gargi Bua hushed him. "Don't ask silly things." Dadi shook her head. "It's not silly. We pray to feel calm and to say thank you for the doctors. Ask me, beta." Jagdish leaned against the bed. "Can I hold the beads next time?"

qa.q: What was Dadi holding in bed?
qa.a: She was holding her prayer beads.

qa.q: How did Jagdish feel when he folded his hands like Dadi?
qa.a: He felt loved and happy to be included, even without knowing why they prayed.

qa.q: What did Dadi do that a wise elder does?
qa.a: She explained simply why they pray and invited more questions instead of hushing him.

qa.q: Why might Gargi Bua react differently from Dadi?
qa.a: She may worry questions are disrespectful in a hospital, or feel anxious about Dadi, so she hushes him.

grounding: A young boy prays with his grandmother in hospital without knowing why, feels included, and she welcomes his questions.
